8304.name: At The Far End Of The Sundered Bridge

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Badlands.

south.description: To the south lies On The Great Northern bridge.

west.description: To the west lies The Badlands.

8304.description:
The great stone bridge ends here on a shelf of cracked grey rock, its
last parapet stones tumbled and split as if some giant fist had struck
them. South, the sundered span leaps back over the roaring gorge toward
the Trade Road. A bleak, wind-scoured waste opens out on either hand,
the badlands running away east and west under a low iron sky. Northward
the ground lifts toward the dark, bare shoulders of the Black Hills.

8305.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies At The Far End Of The Sundered Bridge.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

8305.description:
The first slopes of the Black Hills begin here, low and stony, the soil
between them dark as soot and grown with nothing but wiry grass. A cold
wind pours down from the heights and flattens the grass in grey ripples.
The hills climb north and spread east and west in dull, rounded humps,
while south the land falls back toward the sundered bridge. Somewhere
far off, a crow calls once and is silent.

8306.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

8306.description:
Black shale crunches underfoot on this barren rise, splintered into thin
plates that slide and clatter at every step. From the crest the gorge
behind you shows as a dark scar across the land, and the Spirit Wood as
a smudge of shadow far ahead. Hills roll on north, east and west, and
the slope runs south down toward the bridge country. Nothing grows here
but a crust of grey lichen.

8307.name: The Black Hills

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

8307.description:
A tall cairn of black stones crowns this hilltop, half-collapsed, its
builders long forgotten. The wind keens through the gaps between the
stones with a thin, hollow note that sets your teeth on edge. A sheep
track drops away west along the ridge and another runs east across the
saddle, while the way you came falls south down the shale. Clouds the
colour of wet slate hang low overhead.

extra_descs.cairn black stones:
The cairn was once taller than a man, built of flat black stones fitted
without mortar. A hollow at its heart, now open to the weather, holds
nothing but wind-blown grit and a few green copper stains.

8308.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

8308.description:
The hillside here is scarred by an old landslip, a raw bank of black
earth and boulders that slid down long ago and never healed. Thorny
gorse has taken hold among the stones, its few yellow flowers the only
colour for miles. Paths wind north up the slope and east along the foot
of the slip, while west and south they drop into the hollows between the
hills. The air smells of cold stone and rain.

8309.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

8309.description:
A narrow gully cuts through the hill, its sides streaked black and rust-
red where water has leached the iron from the rock. Pools of brackish
water stand in the bottom, skinned with an oily film. The gully climbs
north toward higher ground and opens south onto the lower slopes, and a
goat path scrambles out of it to the east. Old bleached bones of some
small beast lie wedged among the stones.

8310.name: The Black Hills

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

8310.description:
This is one of the highest of the Black Hills, a bald, windswept dome
where the grass has given up and left only bare dark rock. The wind
never rests up here, and it pushes at you like an unfriendly hand. Far
ahead a grey line of trees marks the edge of the Spirit Wood, and beside
it rises a lone hill crowned by a single gaunt shape. The way runs east
along the crown and south down into the gully.

8311.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Hill Of The Hanged Man.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

8311.description:
Several paths meet in a stony hollow between the hills, where a boundary
stone leans at a drunken angle, its carvings worn smooth. North, a
steeper path climbs toward a lonely hilltop where a gallows stands stark
against the clouds. The other ways wander east and west along the folds
of the hills, and south down a scree slope. The ground is trampled and
muddy, as if many feet pass this way, though none linger.

8312.name: The Hill Of The Hanged Man

north.description: To the north lies The Southern Edge Of Spirit Wood.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

8312.description:
An old gallows of black, weather-split timber crowns this bleak hilltop,
its crossbeam still bearing a frayed length of rope that turns slowly in
the wind. The grass around its foot grows thin and pale, and no bird
will settle on the beam. North, the hill falls away to the dark fringe
of the Spirit Wood, and south a path drops back into the Black Hills.
Even by day the air here feels cold and watchful.

extra_descs.gallows rope crossbeam:
The gallows is old enough that its uprights have split from top to
bottom, yet it still stands. The rope on the crossbeam ends in a noose
worn smooth and dark, and it sways even on the stillest days.

8313.name: The Southern Edge Of Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies In Spirit Wood.

south.description: To the south lies The Hill Of The Hanged Man.

8313.description:
Here the open hills give way to the first trees of the Spirit Wood, grey
and crooked, their bark peeling like dead skin. A chill mist lingers
among the trunks even at midday, and the light turns thin and
colourless. The wood thickens to the north, while to the south the hill
of the gallows rises bare and dark. A deep hush lies over everything, as
though the trees are holding their breath.

8314.name: In Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies In Spirit Wood.

south.description: To the south lies The Southern Edge Of Spirit Wood.

8314.description:
The path winds between ancient yews whose branches knit together
overhead into a low, black roof. Pale fungus glimmers on the rotting
stumps, giving off a faint and sickly glow. Now and then a cold breath
of air passes through the trees with no wind to carry it. The trail
continues north deeper into the wood and south toward its edge.

8315.name: In Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies In Spirit Wood.

south.description: To the south lies In Spirit Wood.

8315.description:
Grey moss hangs in long beards from the branches here, stirring gently
though the air is still. The ground is soft and spongy, layered with
years of fallen needles that swallow the sound of your steps. Faint
whispers seem to drift between the trunks, always just too quiet to make
out. The path leads north and south through the gloom.

8316.name: In Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies In Spirit Wood.

south.description: To the south lies In Spirit Wood.

8316.description:
A ring of pale standing stones, none taller than your knee, encircles a
patch of bare earth beside the path. Nothing grows inside the ring, and
frost clings there even when the rest of the wood is merely damp. The
trees press close around it, gnarled and leaning inward. The trail runs
north between the trunks and south back toward the edge of the wood.

extra_descs.ring standing stones:
Each stone is cut with a single shallow mark, a hand with fingers
spread, worn almost away. Touching one leaves your fingers numb with
cold for a long while after.

8317.name: In Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies In Spirit Wood.

east.description: To the east lies In Spirit Wood.

south.description: To the south lies In Spirit Wood.

west.description: To the west lies In Spirit Wood.

8317.description:
Four paths meet beneath a dead oak, a vast and leafless giant whose
branches spread like grasping fingers over the crossing. Strips of faded
cloth are tied to its lowest boughs, prayers or warnings from travellers
long gone. Paths lead off north, east and west into the wood, and south
back toward the hills. The mist gathers thickest here, curling around
the roots.

8318.name: In Spirit Wood

east.description: To the east lies In Spirit Wood.

8318.description:
The path ends at the edge of a sunken hollow full of tangled briars and
dead bracken. In the middle of the hollow stands a lone stone cross,
leaning and green with lichen, its arms broken. No birds sing here, and
even the wind seems to avoid the place. The only way out is back east to
the crossing beneath the dead oak.

extra_descs.cross stone lichen:
Beneath the lichen, letters run down the shaft of the cross: HERE LIES
THE KEEPER OF THE LODGE, WHO WOULD NOT LEAVE. The stone is always cold
and faintly wet to the touch.

8319.name: In Spirit Wood

south.description: To the south lies In Spirit Wood.

down.description: To the down lies The Tunnel.

8319.description:
The path ends in a hollow where the roots of two great trees have heaved
the earth apart, laying bare a square stone hatch set in the ground. The
hatch is bound with rusted iron bands and chained fast, shutting off the
dark tunnel that leads down beneath it. Cold air seeps up through the
cracks around its edges, smelling of damp stone and something older. The
only open way is back south to the crossing.

8320.name: In Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies The Clearing.

west.description: To the west lies In Spirit Wood.

8320.description:
Ferns as tall as a man crowd the path here, their fronds grey with mist
and dripping with cold water. Somewhere among them a brook trickles
unseen. The way bends at this spot, running north toward a lighter patch
in the trees and west back to the dead oak at the crossing. Webs hang
thick between the ferns, beaded with droplets like strings of tiny
pearls.

8321.name: The Clearing

north.description: To the north lies Deeper In Spirit Wood.

east.description: To the east lies A Small Pond.

south.description: To the south lies In Spirit Wood.

west.description: To the west lies The Camp.

8321.description:
The trees draw back to leave a round clearing open to a grey and
cheerless sky, carpeted with pale, wiry grass. A blackened ring of fire-
stones sits at its centre, cold and long unused. Paths leave the
clearing on every side: north deeper into the wood, east toward the
gleam of a small pond, west toward an old camp, and south back among the
ferns. The silence here feels heavier than among the trees.

8322.name: Deeper In Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies Deep In Spirit Wood.

east.description: To the east lies Deep In Spirit Wood.

south.description: To the south lies The Clearing.

west.description: To the west lies At The Fallen Tree.

8322.description:
The trees grow huge and close here, their trunks black with damp and
their roots coiling over the ground like sleeping serpents. Very little
light reaches the forest floor, and what does is grey and cold. Faint
trails wind north and east into deeper shadow, west toward a great
fallen trunk, and south back to the clearing. A low moaning seems to
rise and fall among the branches, though no wind blows.

8323.name: A Small Pond

west.description: To the west lies The Clearing.

8323.description:
A small, still pond lies in a hollow among the trees, its water black
and glassy and ringed with pale reeds. The reflections in it are
strangely clear, showing the trees, the grey sky, and sometimes shapes
that are not there when you look up. Mist curls across the surface in
thin, slow wisps. A path leads back west to the clearing.

8324.name: The Camp

east.description: To the east lies The Clearing.

8324.description:
An abandoned camp lies under the trees here: a ring of stones around
cold ashes, a lean-to of rotting branches, and the frayed remains of a
canvas awning. Whoever camped here left in a hurry, for a blackened iron
tripod still stands over the dead fire. The ground is scattered with the
prints of boots, all leading away. The clearing lies back to the east.

8325.name: Deep In Spirit Wood

south.description: To the south lies Deeper In Spirit Wood.

8325.description:
The trail dies away among roots and brambles in a dead-end hollow where
the trees stand so close that their trunks form a wall. Hundreds of
small bones have been woven into the brambles, and they click faintly
together whenever the mist stirs. The cold here bites through cloth and
skin alike, and your breath smokes in the gloom. The only way out is
back south through the dark trees.

8326.name: At The Fallen Tree

east.description: To the east lies Deeper In Spirit Wood.

8326.description:
A colossal tree has fallen across the forest floor here, tearing up a
great wheel of roots and earth that stands taller than a house. Its
trunk, furred with moss and riddled with holes, blocks the way beyond.
The hollow beneath the roots draws the eye, a darkness deeper than the
shadows around it. The only path leads back east toward the deeper wood.

8327.name: Deep In Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies In Spirit Wood.

east.description: To the east lies Deeper Into Spirit Wood.

west.description: To the west lies Deeper In Spirit Wood.

8327.description:
A sluggish black stream creeps through the roots here, so still and dark
that it mirrors the branches above like a sheet of polished jet. Its
banks are crusted with pale fungus that crumbles at a touch. A path
follows the water east, another climbs north over a rise of roots, and a
third leads west into the shadowed heart of the wood. The smell of rot
hangs thick in the damp air.

8329.name: Deeper Into Spirit Wood

east.description: To the east lies Deeper Into Spirit Wood.

west.description: To the west lies Deep In Spirit Wood.

8329.description:
A narrow track follows the bank of a dark stream through the trees, the
water sliding past without a sound. Gnarled alders lean out over it,
their roots trailing in the current like drowned hair. The track runs
east toward a faint smell of woodsmoke, and west back toward the heart
of the wood. Pale lights seem to drift above the water, vanishing
whenever you look straight at them.

8330.name: Deeper Into Spirit Wood

east.description: To the east lies At The Forest Lodge.

west.description: To the west lies Deeper Into Spirit Wood.

8330.description:
The trees here bear old axe-marks, and many have been felled, leaving a
scattering of grey stumps among the living trunks. A cart track, deeply
rutted and overgrown with moss, leads east toward a building half-hidden
among the trees. West, the stream-side track winds back into deeper
shadow. Rows of cut logs lie rotting where they were stacked long ago.

8331.name: At The Forest Lodge

east.description: To the east lies Inside The Forest Lodge.

west.description: To the west lies Deeper Into Spirit Wood.

8331.description:
A long, low lodge of dark logs stands in a small clearing here, its roof
of mossy shingles sagging and its chimney leaning. The heavy wooden door
to the east is shut, its iron latch red with rust. Antlers are nailed
above the doorway, bleached white by the weather. West, the cart track
leads back into the trees of the Spirit Wood.

8332.name: In Spirit Wood

east.description: To the east lies In Spirit Wood.

south.description: To the south lies Deep In Spirit Wood.

8332.description:
The trees thin a little here, and grey light filters down through a
ragged gap in the canopy. Thistles and nettles grow rank along the path,
their leaves furred with mildew. A crooked wooden post stands at the
bend, its carved pointer long since rotted away. The path turns east
along a low bank and south back down into the deep wood.

8333.name: In Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies The Northern Edge Of Spirit Wood.

west.description: To the west lies In Spirit Wood.

8333.description:
Birches begin to appear among the darker trees, their white trunks
scarred with black marks like closed eyes. The mist is thinner here, and
the air smells faintly of open ground. North, daylight shows between the
trunks where the wood comes to an end, and west the path winds back
among the yews. A broken fence of split rails runs a little way beside
the trail, then gives up.

8334.name: The Northern Edge Of Spirit Wood

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies In Spirit Wood.

8334.description:
The Spirit Wood ends abruptly at a low bank, and beyond it a wide, grey
grassland stretches north beneath an enormous sky. Wind sweeps across
the open ground, bringing the smell of dust and dry grass. Behind you
the trees stand in a dark, silent wall, the path vanishing south into
their shadow. A weathered stake topped with an animal skull marks the
place where the trail leaves the wood.

8335.name: Inside The Forest Lodge

east.description: To the east lies Behind The Forest Lodge.

west.description: To the west lies At The Forest Lodge.

down.description: To the down lies The Cellar.

8335.description:
The lodge is one long room, dim and cold, with a great stone hearth at
one end and heavy trestle tables along the walls. Animal pelts, stiff
and moth-eaten, hang from the rafters among strings of long-dried herbs.
A trapdoor in the floor opens on a ladder leading down into the cellar,
and a back door stands in the east wall. West, the front door leads out
to the clearing. Everything is coated in fine grey dust, as though no
one has lived here for years.

8336.name: Behind The Forest Lodge

west.description: To the west lies Inside The Forest Lodge.

8336.description:
Behind the lodge lies a small yard, enclosed by the trees and choked
with weeds. A woodpile has collapsed against the wall, and an old
chopping block still holds a rusted axe-head driven deep into its grain.
Beyond the yard the Spirit Wood presses close and dark, with no path
leading into it. The lodge's back door, to the west, is the only way
out.

8337.name: The Cellar

up.description: To the up lies Inside The Forest Lodge.

8337.description:
The cellar is a low, earth-walled room that smells of damp and old
decay. Broken barrels and empty shelves line the walls, and a few
shrivelled roots still hang from hooks in the beams. In one corner the
floor has been dug up and roughly filled in again, the earth mounded
like a grave. A ladder leads up through the trapdoor into the lodge
above.

extra_descs.mound earth grave corner:
The earth is loose and dark, as if it was turned not so long ago. A
wooden spoon has been pushed upright into the top of the mound, like a
marker, and the cold that rises from it is far deeper than the cellar's.

8338.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Northern Edge Of Spirit Wood.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8338.description:
Flat, dun-coloured grassland runs away on every side, broken only by
clumps of thornbush and the odd grey boulder. The grass is short and
brittle, cropped close by wind and beasts. Faint tracks lead north, east
and west across the plains, and south the ground slopes gently down
toward the edge of the Spirit Wood. The sky is huge and colourless,
pressing down on the land like a lid.

8339.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Mountain Trail.

east.description: To the east lies The Icy Claw Of Malebranche.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8339.description:
The plains begin to rise here toward the mountains, the grass giving way
to stony ground scattered with lichen-crusted rocks. North, a trail
heads toward the mountain wall, a dark rampart of cliffs filling the
horizon. East, the icy claw glitters coldly above the grass, while the
open plain stretches south and west. The wind carries a faint smell of
smoke from somewhere unseen.

8340.name: The Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8340.description:
Deep in the thorn thicket the light turns dim and grey, and the branches
knit overhead into a prickly roof. Tufts of coarse fur hang caught on
the thorns at the height of a man's waist. A path through the thicket
leads east back toward open ground, west deeper among the thorns, and
south along a beaten track. A sour animal smell hangs in the still air.

8341.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8341.description:
Stunted thorn trees crowd together here in a thicket that has crept out
across the plains, their branches black and knotted. The ground beneath
them is bare and littered with dead thorns. Narrow ways wind through the
thicket north and west, and out onto the open grass east and south. The
trees creak and rattle in the wind like old bones.

8342.name: The Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

8342.description:
The thicket grows densest here, the thorn trees so tangled that they
form a living wall. A hollow has been hacked into their midst, roofed
with cut branches and floored with trampled earth. Ways lead east
through the thorns and south toward the edge of the plains. The branches
have been scratched with crude marks like claws or tally strokes.

8343.name: The Mountain Trail

north.description: To the north lies The Mountain Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

8343.description:
A stony trail climbs into the foothills, winding between boulders and
stunted, wind-twisted pines. The plains spread out behind you, grey and
endless, as the trail runs south back down to them. North it climbs on
toward the cliffs. Loose rock clatters down from somewhere above, and
the echoes take a long time to die.

8344.name: The Mountain Trail

east.description: To the east lies The Mountain Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The Mountain Trail.

8344.description:
The trail turns sharply here around a great buttress of dark rock, its
face scored with the marks of old tools. A cold spring trickles from the
base of the cliff into a stone basin, cut long ago to catch the water.
The trail continues east along the foot of the mountain and back south
toward the plains. Moss grows thick and green around the basin, the only
soft thing in sight.

8345.name: The Mountain Trail

west.description: To the west lies The Mountain Trail.

up.description: To the up lies Climbing The Mountain Wall.

8345.description:
The trail ends against the sheer face of the mountain wall, a vast cliff
of black rock that rises until it is lost in cloud. Iron pegs and worn
handholds lead up the face, the only way onward. West, the trail runs
back along the foot of the cliffs. Fallen stones litter the ground here,
some of them stained dark.

8346.name: Climbing The Mountain Wall

up.description: To the up lies On A Small Landing.

down.description: To the down lies The Mountain Trail.

8346.description:
You cling to the mountain wall with the wind tearing at your clothes and
nothing beneath your heels but empty air. Rusted iron pegs, hammered
into the rock long ago, offer holds that creak alarmingly under your
weight. The pegs lead up toward a ledge above and down to the trail at
the cliff's foot. Far below, the plains lie spread out like a grey and
faded map.

8347.name: On A Small Landing

east.description: To the east lies The Small Crevice.

up.description: To the up lies The Dark Pillars.

down.description: To the down lies Climbing The Mountain Wall.

8347.description:
A narrow landing juts from the cliff face, barely wide enough to stand
on, its edge crumbling into the void. A dark crack opens in the rock to
the east, just large enough to squeeze into. More pegs lead up toward
the heights, where black shapes like columns stand against the clouds,
and down the cliff toward the trail. Wind roars past the landing in
sudden, buffeting gusts.

8348.name: The Dark Pillars

east.description: To the east lies On The Mountain Road.

down.description: To the down lies On A Small Landing.

west.description: To the west lies Going Up The Winding Mountain-trail.

8348.description:
Tall pillars of black basalt rise from a bare plateau here, dozens of
them, standing in silent rows like an army of giants turned to stone.
Their surfaces are glassy and cold, and nothing grows in their shadows.
A mountain road leads away east between the last of the pillars, and
west a dark opening leads into a winding trail inside the mountain. The
pegs on the cliff lead down to a small landing below.

extra_descs.pillars basalt black:
Each pillar has six flat sides, as if cut by a mason, though no tool
could have shaped so many. Close up, faint reflections move in their
glassy surfaces a moment after you do.

8349.name: On The Mountain Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Mountain Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dark Pillars.

8349.description:
A broad road of fitted stones runs across the high plateau, its paving
cracked and heaved by frost. On either side the ground is bare grey
rock, without soil or grass. North, the road climbs toward a gap between
two peaks, and west it runs back among the black pillars. Somewhere
ahead, the wind howls through a narrow place.

8350.name: On The Mountain Road

north.description: To the north lies At The Bridge Of Death.

south.description: To the south lies On The Mountain Road.

8350.description:
The road climbs steadily between rising walls of rock, and the air grows
thin and bitterly cold. Old cairns mark the way at intervals, each
topped with a white stone. North, a deep chasm opens across the road
ahead, and south the road leads back down toward the plateau. Snow lies
in the cracks of the paving and in the lee of every boulder.

8353.name: At The Bridge Of Death

north.description: To the north lies Crossing A Narrow Stone Bridge.

south.description: To the south lies On The Mountain Road.

8353.description:
The road ends at the brink of a terrible ravine, so deep that its bottom
is lost in mist and shadow. Spanning it is a stone bridge no wider than
a man's shoulders, without rail or wall, arching north over the abyss
toward the far side. A weathered stone stands at the bridge's head,
carved with a skull and a warning. South, the road leads back down
between the peaks.

extra_descs.stone warning skull:
Beneath the carved skull, letters in an old hand read: ONE AT A TIME,
AND DO NOT LOOK DOWN. Someone has added a long list of names below, each
crossed through.

8354.name: Crossing A Narrow Stone Bridge

north.description: To the north lies On The Far Side Of The Ravine.

south.description: To the south lies At The Bridge Of Death.

8354.description:
You edge along the narrow stone bridge with nothing on either side but a
sickening drop into mist and darkness. The wind shrieks up out of the
ravine, snatching at you and trying to pull you off your feet. The far
side lies north, and the bridge's head back south, both seeming
impossibly far away. Small stones break from the span beneath your feet
and fall without a sound.

8355.name: On The Far Side Of The Ravine

south.description: To the south lies Crossing A Narrow Stone Bridge.

up.description: To the up lies Before The Dark Castle.

8355.description:
The narrow bridge comes to rest on a ledge of black rock at the far side
of the ravine. A steep, crooked stair is cut into the cliff above,
leading up toward a dark mass of walls and towers that loom against the
clouds. South, the bridge stretches back over the abyss. The stones of
the ledge are cold and slick with mist.

8356.name: The Small Crevice

north.description: To the north lies A Cave Room.

west.description: To the west lies On A Small Landing.

8356.description:
This crevice is a tight crack in the mountain, its rough walls pressing
in on both sides and its ceiling lost in blackness. The air is still and
stale, and the only light comes from the landing to the west. North, the
crevice narrows to a gap choked with fallen rock and closed by an old
iron grille, beyond which some cave lies in darkness. Scratches in the
stone near the grille look like the work of fingernails.

8357.name: Before The Dark Castle

south.description: To the south lies The Castle Yard.

down.description: To the down lies On The Far Side Of The Ravine.

8357.description:
A grim castle of black stone rises before you, its walls sheer and
windowless, its towers lost in low, smoky cloud. The great gate stands
to the south, a portcullis of iron bars rusted into place and shut fast,
barring the way into the castle yard. Below the walls, the crooked stair
leads down to the ledge above the ravine. No banner flies and no light
shows, but the place does not feel empty.

9100.name: The Badlands

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Badlands.

west.description: To the west lies At The Far End Of The Sundered Bridge.

9100.description:
The badlands stretch out bare and cracked here, a wasteland of grey clay
furrowed by countless dry gullies. A few dead shrubs cling on in the
shelter of the ridges. Westward lies the end of the sundered bridge,
eastward the waste continues, and north the ground rises toward the
Black Hills. The ground is so dry that every step raises a puff of fine
dust.

9101.name: The Badlands

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Badlands.

9101.description:
Strange towers of eroded clay rise from the badlands here, sculpted by
wind and rain into fantastic shapes like melted candles. Between them
the ground is a maze of narrow gullies. The way leads north toward the
hills and west across the waste. The wind whistles through the clay
towers with an eerie, mournful sound.

9102.name: The Badlands

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies At The Far End Of The Sundered Bridge.

west.description: To the west lies The Badlands.

9102.description:
The badlands are at their bleakest here, a plain of cracked grey clay
where nothing grows at all. The cracks are wide enough to swallow a
foot, and the ground rings hollow underfoot. East lies the end of the
sundered bridge and west the waste runs on, while north the ground rises
toward the hills. The sky hangs low and grey, threatening a rain that
never comes.

9103.name: The Badlands

east.description: To the east lies The Badlands.

9103.description:
The badlands end here at the brink of the great gorge, a sheer drop into
a roaring chasm where the river runs far below. There is no way down,
and the far side is a distant wall of rock. The only path leads back
east across the cracked clay. Spray from the river rises on the wind,
leaving a fine wet sheen on the rocks.

9104.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Badlands.

9104.description:
The hillside here is cut into rough terraces, perhaps fields once, now
gone to coarse grass and bramble. Low walls of stacked stones hold up
the terraces, bulging and slipping under the weight of earth. Paths lead
north along the hillside, east toward the first slopes of the hills, and
south down to the badlands. The air is heavy with the smell of rain.

9105.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Badlands.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9105.description:
The lower slopes of the Black Hills are scarred here by gullies where
the rain has torn the thin soil away from the dark rock. Bare stones jut
up through the turf like old broken teeth. Ways climb north into the
hills, run east and west along the slopes, and fall south toward the
badlands. The land is quiet but for the wind and the trickle of hidden
water.

9106.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Badlands.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9106.description:
Four sheep-tracks meet here beside a crude shrine of stacked stones,
daubed with faded ochre signs. A hollow in the shrine is crusted with
old candle wax and green smears where coins once lay, offerings to
whatever watches over these hills. Tracks lead north into the hills,
east toward the edge of a ravine, west across the slopes, and south down
toward the badlands. The wind tugs at a tattered rag tied to the topmost
stone.

9107.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9107.description:
The moorland ends at the brink of a steep drop, where the land falls
away into a deep, mist-filled ravine. Far across the gulf, the dim
shapes of mountains rise in ragged ranks. Paths lead north along the
edge and west back across the moor. The wind rising from the ravine is
wet and cold and smells of distant snow.

9108.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9108.description:
A shallow stream crosses the moor here over a bed of black stones, its
water stained the colour of strong tea. Stepping stones, set long ago,
lead across it, some of them now tilted or sunk. Paths run north and
south along the stream, and west up a gentle rise. Tufts of bog cotton
nod white along the banks.

9109.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9109.description:
A lone, lightning-blasted thorn tree stands on the moor here, its trunk
split in two and charred black. The wind has bent it until its branches
all point the same way, like a hand warning you back. Paths lead north
and south across the open ground, and west into a hollow between the
hills. Old rooks' nests, long deserted, clot the dead branches.

9110.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9110.description:
The upland here is cut by old peat diggings, square black pits half full
of brown water. Abandoned turves lie stacked and crumbling beside them.
Paths wander north and south across the moor, and west toward the higher
hills. The smell of wet earth and peat smoke hangs over the place,
though no fire burns.

9111.name: The Black Hills

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9111.description:
The hills flatten out into a bleak upland of coarse grass and black,
peaty pools. A tumbledown wall of dry stones runs across the moor, built
by hands long gone and now good for nothing but shelter from the wind.
Paths lead south across the upland and west toward a rocky ridge. The
pools reflect a sky the colour of ashes.

9112.name: The Black Hills

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9112.description:
A long ridge of black rock runs along the top of the hills here like the
spine of some buried beast. From its crest you can see a lonely gallows
on a hilltop, and beyond it the grey sprawl of the Spirit Wood. The
ridge path runs east and west, and a stony way drops south into a
sheltered hollow. The wind moans through the cracks in the rock.

9113.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9113.description:
A broad, flat-topped hill rises here, its summit strewn with the tumbled
stones of some ancient wall. From the top you can follow the dark hills
rolling away on every side, and see a gash where a ravine cuts across
them. Paths lead north and south over the summit, west toward the
valleys, and east toward a stone gatehouse. Thin, grey grass grows among
the fallen stones.

9114.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9114.description:
The hills crowd together here into a maze of narrow valleys and knobbly
ridges, all of the same dark rock. A trickle of water runs down the
middle of the valley floor, feeding a few ragged ferns. Ways lead off
north toward a stony hollow, east and west along the valley, and south
down a slope of scree. It would be easy to lose your way among these
folds of land.

9115.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9115.description:
A steep, rocky slope rises here, its face pocked with the dark mouths of
small caves and burrows. Loose black scree slides underfoot, and the
climbing is hard going. Paths cross the slope north and south, and run
east and west around its shoulder. A faint, sour smell of animal dens
drifts from the cave mouths.

9116.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9116.description:
A small tarn lies cupped among the hills here, its black water rippling
in the wind. Heather and bilberry grow thickly around its shores, and a
few hardy rowans cling to the rocks. Paths circle the tarn north, south,
east and west, linking the hollows of the hills. The water is so dark
that it seems bottomless.

9117.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9117.description:
A long, gentle slope of rough pasture runs down the hillside here,
crossed by the remains of an old field wall. Thistles and docks have
taken over the pasture, and the wall's stones lie scattered where they
fell. Paths lead north up toward a tarn, east across the slope, and west
toward a grassy saddle. A rusted iron gate hangs from a single post in
the wall, opening onto nothing.

9118.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9118.description:
This broad, grassy saddle between two hills is dotted with grey
boulders, some of them split open by frost. Sheep have worn deep paths
through the turf, though the flocks are long gone. Tracks lead north up
into the higher hills, east and west along the saddle, and south toward
a crossroads shrine. The grass here is short and springy, starred with
tiny white flowers.

9119.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

9119.description:
A flat shelf of land lies between the hills here, covered with coarse
grass and sprinkled with black flints. Ruined sheepfolds stand at
intervals, their walls fallen into low rings of stone. Paths lead north
into the steeper hills, east across the shelf, south toward the lower
slopes and west up a shale rise. Wind hums through the grass with a low,
steady sound.

9120.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

9120.description:
A rough track runs along the hillside here, worn into the soil by
generations of drovers and their herds. A wooden post leans by the way,
notched with old marks that once told the distance to somewhere. The
track runs north and south along the hill, and a path climbs east to the
shale-strewn heights. Black feathers lie scattered in the grass around
the post.

9121.name: The Black Hills

east.description: To the east lies The Black Hills.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

9121.description:
The hills give way here to a high, windy field of thin grass edged with
stones. A fallen standing stone lies half-buried in the turf, its face
carved with spirals that the weather has nearly erased. Paths lead east
toward a cairn-topped hill and south along the hillside. Far away, the
land drops toward a broad, grey valley.

extra_descs.standing stone spirals fallen:
The spirals wind inward to a small hollow at the stone's heart, worn
smooth as if by countless thumbs. Rainwater gathers there and never
quite seems to dry.

9122.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9122.description:
A dry watercourse wanders across the plain here, its bed nothing but
cracked mud and rounded pebbles. Thistles nod along its banks in the
endless wind. Open grassland stretches away north and east, west and
south, without a tree or a roof in sight. Far off, a line of jagged
peaks rises dim and blue beyond the grass.

9123.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Icy Claw Of Malebranche.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9123.description:
The ground hardens here, the grass growing in thin tufts between patches
of bare, frost-split earth. A bitter chill creeps down from the north,
where a great white shape like a crooked claw rises from the plain.
Tracks run east and west across the grass, and south back toward the dry
watercourse. Hoarfrost lingers in the hollows long after dawn.

9124.name: The Icy Claw Of Malebranche

east.description: To the east lies The Rickety-Rope Bridge.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9124.description:
A huge outcrop of rock juts from the plain here, curved like a talon and
sheathed in blue-white ice that never seems to melt. Freezing air flows
down from it in a slow, invisible river, and the grass around its foot
is stiff and white with rime. East, a rope bridge sways across a narrow
ravine, while west and south the frozen plain opens out again. The ice
creaks and groans faintly, as if the claw were flexing.

extra_descs.claw ice outcrop malebranche:
Deep inside the ice, blurred as if seen through cloudy glass, dark
shapes hang frozen: twisted roots, a broken spear, and something that
might once have been a hand. Your own breath frosts the ice when you
lean close.

9125.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9125.description:
A low mound rises from the plain here, covered with coarse grass and
crowned with a ring of upright stones. From its top you can see the dark
mass of the Spirit Wood against the grey land. The plain runs north and
west from the mound, and east toward the path from the wood. Burrows
have been dug deep into the mound's flanks, each ringed with a fan of
pale spoil.

9126.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9126.description:
This corner of the plains is a shallow basin where rainwater collects in
muddy pools and the grass grows longer and greener than elsewhere. The
mud is crossed with paw prints and the sharp slots of hooves. A track
leads north along the basin's rim, and west across the plain toward the
trail from the Spirit Wood. Reeds rattle around the pools in the wind.

9127.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9127.description:
Grey grass ripples away under the wind, and stones lie half-sunk in the
earth like the backs of drowned beasts. Animal trails wander through the
grass, north toward the ravine and south across the open ground. A wider
track leads west toward the middle of the plains. The sky is empty and
grey, without even a bird to break it.

9128.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Rickety-Rope Bridge.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9128.description:
The plain runs up to the edge of a narrow ravine here, a deep crack in
the earth whose far side lies only a stone's throw away. North, a rope
bridge sways over the gap. Tracks run south across the grass and west
toward the open plain. Tough little shrubs cling to the ravine's lip,
bent flat by the wind.

9129.name: The Rickety-Rope Bridge

east.description: To the east lies The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Icy Claw Of Malebranche.

9129.description:
A flimsy bridge of fraying rope and warped planks sways across a deep,
narrow ravine, creaking with every gust. Through the gaps between the
boards you can see the stony floor of the gorge far below, and the drop
tugs at your stomach. The bridge leads east to an old gravel road and
back west to the icy claw, while a trampled path follows the near rim of
the ravine south. Several planks are missing altogether.

9130.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

9130.description:
This is the edge of the open plains, where the grass grows waist-high
and grey and hisses ceaselessly in the wind. Hidden hollows and old pits
make every step uncertain. Paths have been beaten through the grass
north and east. Beyond the grass the land rolls away, empty and grey, to
a horizon smudged with dust.

9131.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9131.description:
The grass thins here into a stretch of hard-packed earth trampled by
many feet, and the ashes of a recent fire lie in a blackened circle.
Shards of broken pots and gnawed bones are trodden into the dirt around
it. North, scrubby trees mark the start of a thicket; tracks lead east
and south across the grass, and west toward a barricade on the horizon.
The place stinks of smoke and of something rank and animal.

9132.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9132.description:
The plains here are scarred by a wide burn, the grass reduced to black
stubble and the earth crusted with ash. The smell of old smoke still
clings to the ground. Grassland stretches unburned to the north and
east, south and west, around the edges of the black patch. Charred bones
of some large beast lie at the heart of the burn.

9133.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

9133.description:
Tufts of grey grass and low, spiny bushes cover the plain, and the earth
between them is cracked into a pattern of dry plates. A ruined
shepherd's hut of piled stones stands roofless here, its doorway facing
the wind. Tracks lead north toward the foothills, east across the plain,
south over the grass and west toward a dark line of trees. Tattered
strips of hide flap from a pole beside the hut.

9134.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies Entrance To The Draconian Encampment.

9134.description:
The plains end here against a crude barricade of sharpened stakes and
heaped thornbrush that runs across the land as far as you can see.
Beyond it, to the west, rises the smoke of many fires, but the only gap
in the barricade is blocked by a heavy timber gate lashed shut with
rawhide. North and east, the grass stretches back across the open
plains. Skulls of beasts and men are spiked along the tops of the
stakes.

9135.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

9135.description:
The thorn thicket gives way here to open grassland that slopes gently
down toward a wide hollow. Wind-blown seeds drift through the air like
grey snow. North, the thorns close in again; east, a path skirts the
thicket's edge; and south, the grass runs on toward a palisade of
stakes. Hoofprints and broad, clawed footprints are pressed together in
the soft ground.

9143.name: Crossing The Dark Plains

north.description: To the north lies Crossing The Dark Plains.

9143.description:
The path across the dark plains ends at a shallow pit in the cavern
floor, ringed with stones and filled with ancient ash and charred bones.
The darkness is absolute beyond the reach of your light, and the silence
feels like a held breath. The little cairns lead back north across the
cavern toward the winding trail. A cold draught rises from the pit,
carrying the smell of old smoke.

9144.name: Crossing The Dark Plains

north.description: To the north lies Crossing The Dark Plains.

south.description: To the south lies Crossing The Dark Plains.

9144.description:
Out on the dark plains the walls of the cavern have vanished altogether,
and the darkness presses in on every side. The floor is fine black grit,
crisscrossed with old footprints that lead nowhere in particular. The
line of little cairns runs north toward the passage and south deeper
into the cavern. A faint sound like distant breathing rises and falls in
the blackness.

9145.name: Crossing The Dark Plains

north.description: To the north lies Going Up The Winding Mountain-trail.

south.description: To the south lies Crossing The Dark Plains.

9145.description:
The passage opens onto the edge of a vast cavern whose floor stretches
away flat and featureless into utter darkness, like a plain beneath a
starless night. Somewhere high above, the unseen roof drips, and the
drops fall a very long way. North, the winding trail begins its climb
out of the cavern, and south a faint path marked by small stone cairns
leads across the dark plains. The cold here is deep and still.

9146.name: Going Up The Winding Mountain-trail

north.description: To the north lies Going Up The Winding Mountain-trail.

south.description: To the south lies Crossing The Dark Plains.

9146.description:
The passage climbs in long, tight curves, the floor cut into shallow
steps that are slick with seepage. The walls press close and the ceiling
hangs low, forcing you to stoop in places. North, the trail winds on
toward a faint grey light, and south it descends into an immense
darkness. Your breathing sounds very loud in the narrow space.

9147.name: Going Up The Winding Mountain-trail

north.description: To the north lies The Dark Pillars.

south.description: To the south lies Going Up The Winding Mountain-trail.

east.description: To the east lies The Dark Pillars.

9147.description:
A trail winds through the inside of the mountain along a passage worn
smooth by water and feet, its walls glistening black in the faint light.
Daylight leaks in ahead, where the passage forks and both openings,
north and east, come out among the dark pillars. South, the trail
spirals back down into darkness. The air smells of wet stone and cold
iron.

9156.name: The Frozen Trail

north.description: To the north lies The Frozen Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The Trail Along The Dim Stairs.

9156.description:
The tunnel stair opens onto a trail along a bare mountainside, deep in
old snow and glazed with ice. The wind howls across the slope, flinging
needles of frost into your face. The trail climbs north along the
mountain, and south it ducks back into the dim stairs. Far below, the
lake lies like a dark mirror among the peaks.

9157.name: The Frozen Trail

north.description: To the north lies The Frozen Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The Frozen Trail.

9157.description:
The frozen trail edges along a ledge where the snow has been packed into
treacherous ice. Icicles as long as spears hang from the overhanging
rock, dripping in the rare moments of sun. North the trail continues to
climb, and south it winds back toward the stair. Every step must be
tested before you trust your weight to it.

9158.name: The Frozen Trail

south.description: To the south lies The Frozen Trail.

up.description: To the up lies The Frozen Trail.

9158.description:
The trail comes to the foot of an icy slope too steep to walk, where
steps have been cut into the frozen snow and a frayed rope is pegged
alongside them. The way up climbs toward a high shoulder of the
mountain. South, the trail runs back along the ledge. The cold here is
fierce enough to make your fingers ache inside your gloves.

9159.name: The Frozen Trail

east.description: To the east lies Durgar's Gate - The Doors To The Dwarven Kingdom.

down.description: To the down lies The Frozen Trail.

9159.description:
Atop the icy slope the trail levels out onto a broad shoulder of the
mountain, swept nearly bare by a fierce, unending wind. East, a road of
carved flagstones leads toward a great doorway set in the mountain's
flank. The cut steps lead down the slope behind you. Rime feathers every
rock, glittering in the thin light.

9160.name: Durgar's Gate - The Doors To The Dwarven Kingdom

north.description: To the north lies Durgan's Gate.

west.description: To the west lies The Frozen Trail.

9160.description:
Two immense doors of dark iron and stone are set into the mountainside
here, carved with rows of bearded kings and bound with bands of
tarnished bronze. This is Durgar's Gate, the way into the dwarven
kingdom, and its doors lead north into the mountain, though they stand
shut and barred, their great hinges locked with ice. Runes run around
the arch above in a deep-cut band. West, the frozen trail leads back
along the shoulder of the mountain.

extra_descs.runes arch band:
The runes are dwarven and cut as deep as a finger. Those who can read
them make out a name, Durgar, and a warning that the mountain keeps what
it is given.

9161.name: The Canyon Of Khel-zaram

north.description: To the north lies The Canyon Of Khel-zaram.

south.description: To the south lies The Old Watchtower.

9161.description:
The path enters the Canyon of Khel-zaram between walls of banded red and
ochre rock that rise sheer for hundreds of feet. Only a narrow strip of
sky shows overhead, and the canyon floor lies in cold shadow. North, the
gorge winds on between the cliffs, and south the path climbs back out to
the watchtower. Your voice comes back from the walls in strange, broken
echoes.

9162.name: The Canyon Of Khel-zaram

north.description: To the north lies The Canyon Of Khel-zaram.

south.description: To the south lies The Canyon Of Khel-zaram.

9162.description:
Boulders the size of cottages have fallen from the cliffs and lie
jumbled across the canyon floor, leaving only a twisting path between
them. Carvings of bearded faces, worn almost smooth, peer out from the
rock walls at the height of a man. The canyon runs on north between the
cliffs and back south toward its mouth. A thin trickle of water drips
somewhere among the stones.

extra_descs.carvings faces bearded:
The faces are dwarven, broad and solemn, with braided beards that fall
into knotwork borders. Each wears a different crown, and each has had
its eyes chiselled out by some later, angrier hand.

9163.name: The Canyon Of Khel-zaram

east.description: To the east lies The Vale of Dim Streams.

south.description: To the south lies The Canyon Of Khel-zaram.

9163.description:
The canyon ends against a towering wall of red rock streaked with white
mineral stains, where a cold spring seeps from a crack and spreads
across the floor. Here the path turns east, following the water out
through a gap into a hidden valley. South, the canyon winds back between
its cliffs. The air is damp and cool, and moss grows thick wherever the
water runs.

9164.name: The Vale of Dim Streams

north.description: To the north lies Along The Shores Of Lake Zaram.

west.description: To the west lies The Canyon Of Khel-zaram.

9164.description:
A small, deep valley opens among the mountains, its floor laced with a
dozen shallow streams that wander and braid through beds of grey
shingle. Mist hangs low over the water, and the light here is soft and
dim even at noon. North, the streams gather toward the shore of a still
mountain lake, while west a gap in the rock leads back into the canyon.
The murmur of running water fills the vale.

9165.name: Along The Shores Of Lake Zaram

south.description: To the south lies The Vale of Dim Streams.

west.description: To the west lies The Trail Along The Dim Stairs.

9165.description:
The dark waters of Lake Zaram lie still and cold beneath the peaks, so
clear that pale stones show far beneath the surface. A narrow beach of
black pebbles curves along the shore, crunching underfoot. West, a
flight of rough steps disappears into a cleft in the mountainside, and
south the shore leads back down into the vale of streams. No ripple
stirs the water, and nothing rises to break it.

9166.name: The Trail Along The Dim Stairs

north.description: To the north lies The Trail Along The Dim Stairs.

east.description: To the east lies Along The Shores Of Lake Zaram.

9166.description:
A stair of rough-hewn steps enters the mountain through a tunnel barely
wider than your shoulders. What little light there is filters in from
the lake shore to the east, fading to a dim grey glow on the damp walls.
The steps go on north into deeper darkness. Water drips steadily from
the ceiling, and each drop echoes like a footstep.

9167.name: The Trail Along The Dim Stairs

north.description: To the north lies The Frozen Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The Trail Along The Dim Stairs.

9167.description:
The dim stairs wind on through the heart of the rock, the steps slick
with icy water and worn smooth by countless feet. Iron rings are set
into the wall at intervals, rusted into lumps, where torches may once
have burned. A breath of freezing air comes down from the north, where
the stair rises toward the open mountainside. South, the steps descend
toward the lake.

9168.name: The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Rickety-Rope Bridge.

9168.description:
An old road of packed grey gravel begins at the end of the rope bridge
and strikes out east across a flat, lifeless plain. Its edges are lined
with half-buried kerbstones, cut long ago by careful hands. Westward the
rope bridge creaks over the ravine. Nothing grows beside the road but a
few dead stalks rattling in the wind.

9169.name: The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains.

9169.description:
The desolated plains stretch flat and featureless on both sides of the
road, a waste of grey dust and cracked clay without a single blade of
grass. The wind lifts the dust in slow, twisting columns that wander
across the land and fall apart. The gravel road runs straight as a spear
east and west. Your footsteps crunch loudly in the vast silence.

9170.name: The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains.

9170.description:
A milestone stands beside the road here, a squat pillar of granite whose
carvings have been scoured away by grit until only a faint pointing hand
remains. Around it the plain is strewn with white stones like scattered
teeth. The road goes on east toward distant hills and west toward the
ravine. The sun, when it shows at all, is a pale coin behind the haze.

extra_descs.milestone pillar granite hand:
Only the carved hand survives, its finger pointing along the road toward
the hills. Someone has scratched a tally of short lines beneath it,
dozens of them, as if counting days or the dead.

9171.name: The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Old Gravel Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains.

9171.description:
The remains of a wagon lie in the ditch beside the road, its wheels
broken and its timbers bleached silver by sun and wind. Whatever it once
carried was taken long ago. Ahead the road begins to curve east toward
rising ground, and behind you it runs back west across the empty plain.
Dust has drifted in a soft grey bank against the wreck's side.

9172.name: The Old Gravel Road

north.description: To the north lies The Old Gravel Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Old Gravel Road Crossing The Desolated Plains.

9172.description:
The gravel road bends sharply here, turning north toward the foothills
where the ground starts to buckle and climb. Banks of loose scree spill
onto the road from a low cut in the land. Westward it runs back across
the desolated plains toward the rope bridge. A cold wind smelling of
snow comes down from the heights.

9173.name: The Old Gravel Road

south.description: To the south lies The Old Gravel Road.

up.description: To the up lies The Old Gravel Road.

9173.description:
The road reaches the foot of a steep slope and climbs it by rough steps
cut into the rock, each one worn into a shallow bowl. The way up leads
to a higher stretch of road along the hillside. South, the road runs
back to its bend at the edge of the plains. Hardy thornbushes cling to
the bank, their branches hung with tufts of grey wool.

9174.name: The Old Gravel Road

north.description: To the north lies The Old Gravel Road.

down.description: To the down lies The Old Gravel Road.

9174.description:
The road runs along a shelf cut into the hillside, with a sheer drop on
one hand and a wall of crumbling rock on the other. Below, the rough
steps lead down toward the plains, which spread away grey and endless
beyond the foothills. North, the road continues along the shelf,
climbing gently. Loose stones skitter away under your feet and vanish
over the edge.

9175.name: The Old Gravel Road

east.description: To the east lies The Old Gravel Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Old Gravel Road.

9175.description:
The shelf widens into a level stretch of road, paved here with big flat
slabs where the gravel has washed away. Old wheel ruts are worn deep
into the stone, filled now with rainwater and dead leaves. The road
turns east toward a dark tower that rises on a spur above the hills, and
back south along the hillside. The wind has an edge of ice to it now.

9176.name: The Old Gravel Road

west.description: To the west lies The Old Gravel Road.

up.description: To the up lies The Old Watchtower.

9176.description:
The road ends below a rocky spur, and a steep track zigzags up toward
the grim old watchtower that crowns it. The tower's walls are dark with
age, and the empty slits of its windows gaze down at you. West, the
paved road runs back along the hillside. Thorn and bramble choke the
foot of the slope, leaving only the narrow track clear.

9177.name: The Old Watchtower

north.description: To the north lies The Canyon Of Khel-zaram.

east.description: To the east lies Inside The Old Watchtower.

down.description: To the down lies The Old Gravel Road.

9177.description:
You stand on the windswept summit of the spur, at the foot of an old
watchtower built of rough black stone. Its doorway gapes open to the
east, the door long gone, and arrow slits stare out over the land below.
North, a narrow path leads into the mouth of a deep canyon between
towering walls of red rock. The track drops back down toward the road
beneath the spur.

9178.name: Inside The Old Watchtower

west.description: To the west lies The Old Watchtower.

up.description: To the up lies The Look-Out.

9178.description:
The inside of the watchtower is a single round chamber, its stone floor
littered with fallen plaster and old bird droppings. A cold hearth is
built into one wall, black with soot, and a broken table leans against
another. Narrow stairs spiral up inside the wall toward the look-out
above. West, the empty doorway lets in a grey square of daylight and a
whistle of wind.

9179.name: The Look-Out

down.description: To the down lies Inside The Old Watchtower.

9179.description:
The topmost chamber of the tower is a cramped room ringed by tall window
slits, through which the wind moans and whistles. From here the watchers
of old could see the plains far below, the dark line of the canyon, and
the road snaking off across the waste. Names and dates have been
scratched into the stone sills by long-dead sentries. A narrow stair
leads down into the chamber beneath.

extra_descs.names dates sills scratches:
Dozens of names crowd the sills, some neat, some little more than
scratches. The last one, cut deeper than the rest, is followed by a
single word: alone.

24700.name: The Black Hills

north.description: To the north lies The Black Hills.

east.description: To the east lies Before The Bridge Across The Ravine.

south.description: To the south lies The Black Hills.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

24700.description:
A squat gatehouse of dressed grey stone blocks the way east, built by
dwarven hands into a cleft between two hills. Its heavy oaken door,
bound with iron, stands shut, and the arch above it is carved with a
hammer and an anvil. Paths wander off north, south and west across the
dark hills. The stonework is old but sound, and not a single block has
slipped out of line.

extra_descs.hammer anvil carving arch gatehouse:
The hammer and anvil are cut in the crisp, deep style of dwarven masons,
and beneath them a line of runes names the gatehouse as the Ravine Ward
of Aredrel. The door's iron studs are each shaped like a tiny bearded
face.

24701.name: Before The Bridge Across The Ravine

east.description: To the east lies On The Bridge Across The Ravine.

west.description: To the west lies The Black Hills.

24701.description:
Beyond the gatehouse a paved terrace ends at the brink of a vast ravine,
and a bridge of carved stone leaps out across it toward the far
mountains. A massive iron gate, bolted and chained, closes the bridge's
head to the east, its bars as thick as a man's wrist. West, the door
leads back through the gatehouse to the hills. Mist boils up out of the
ravine, hiding its depths entirely.

647100.name: carrion crow bird black
647100.long_desc: A carrion crow hops along the ground, picking at something you would rather not see.
647100.description:
A big, ragged black crow with a heavy grey beak and dull, knowing eyes.
Its feathers are matted with dust, and it keeps its head cocked toward
you as though weighing how long you might last out here.

647101.name: jackal badland dog
647101.long_desc: A lean badland jackal slinks between the rocks, lips curled back from yellow teeth.
647101.description:
It is a gaunt, sandy-grey dog with oversized ears and ribs that show
plainly through its mangy coat. It moves in a low, sidelong trot and
never quite turns its back on you, and its yellow eyes are bright with
hunger.

647102.name: gnoll raider hyena
647102.long_desc: A gnoll raider prowls here, sniffing the wind and swinging a spiked flail.
647102.description:
A hulking, hyena-headed gnoll stands taller than a man, its spotted hide
covered in scraps of stolen leather and rusted mail. Its muzzle is
scarred and grinning, and it gives off a rank stink of carrion and
smoke. A string of teeth and finger-bones rattles at its neck.

647103.name: hill troll brute
647103.long_desc: A hill troll squats among the rocks, gnawing on a thighbone.
647103.description:
The troll is a stooped mountain of grey-green flesh, its warty hide
crusted with lichen and dirt. Its arms hang nearly to the ground and end
in black, cracked claws, and its small eyes peer out from under a heavy
brow with dull malice.

647104.name: restless spirit ghost pale
647104.long_desc: A restless spirit drifts between the trees, its pale face twisted in sorrow.
647104.description:
It is the grey, half-transparent shape of a man or woman, its features
blurred like a face seen through rain. Its mouth moves endlessly without
a sound, and a bitter cold comes off it, frosting the leaves wherever it
passes. A fine grey ash sifts from its hems as it moves.

647105.name: ghost hanged man
647105.short_desc: the ghost of the hanged man
647105.long_desc: The ghost of the hanged man sways beneath the gallows, a noose still tight about his neck.
647105.description:
He is a grey, gaunt shape in the rags of an old coat, his head bent at a
dreadful angle by the rope that still hangs from his neck. His eyes are
empty hollows, yet they follow you wherever you go. His lips are black,
and when the wind drops you can hear him whispering the name of the man
who hanged him.

647106.name: ghost lodge keeper old man
647106.long_desc: The ghost of the lodge-keeper shuffles about his old haunts, holding up a dim lantern.
647106.description:
A stooped old man in a leather apron and a woodsman's hood, all of him
grey and faint as smoke. He lifts his lantern to peer at each visitor in
turn, and his face crumples with anger when he finds a stranger. Earth
clings to his hands and knees, as though he dug his own grave.

647107.name: spider web grey giant
647107.long_desc: A grey web spider the size of a dog clings to a tree trunk, its legs folded tight.
647107.description:
Its bloated grey body is furred with bristles and marked with a pale
pattern like a skull. Eight black eyes glitter above a pair of dripping
fangs, and threads of sticky silk trail from its spinnerets wherever it
creeps. It has come out of the dark woods of Haon-Dor, or its mother
did.

647108.name: cultist black robed man
647108.long_desc: A black-robed cultist stands here, chanting softly over a guttering black candle.
647108.description:
His robe is black wool stitched with a spider in silver thread, and his
face is painted grey with ash. His hands are stained with wax and old
blood, and he murmurs the same few words over and over in a tongue you
do not know. He bears the mark of the dark temple of Haon-Dor on the
back of one hand.

747100.name: flail gnoll spiked chain
747100.room_desc: A crude spiked flail lies here, its chain caked with rust.
747100.description: A knotted wooden haft is joined by a length of rusty chain to an iron ball hammered full of crude spikes. It is ugly, heavy and stained with old blood.

747101.name: token rope hangman noose knot
747101.room_desc: A short loop of frayed rope, tied in a hangman's knot, lies here.
747101.description: A hand's length of old, dark rope tied in a perfect hangman's knot, worn smooth by the grip of a dead man's neck. It is always cold, and some say it brings luck to anyone bold enough to carry it.

747102.name: lantern lodge keeper iron horn
747102.room_desc: An old iron lantern with horn panes sits here.
747102.description: A sturdy iron lantern with panes of scraped horn, its handle wrapped in worn leather. Its flame burns low and steady and never seems to need trimming.

747103.name: ash spirit pouch grey
747103.room_desc: A small pouch spilling fine grey ash lies here.
747103.description: A twist of cloth holding a pinch of fine, cold grey ash that never quite settles. Hedge-witches and priests pay well for it.

747104.name: silk spider skein grey
747104.room_desc: A skein of grey spider silk lies here, faintly sticky.
747104.description: A tangle of grey silk as strong as wire and still a little sticky, wound into a rough skein. Weavers prize it for cloth that turns a blade.

747105.name: venom sac spider poison
747105.room_desc: A swollen, glistening venom sac lies here.
747105.description: A bulging sac of dark venom cut from a giant spider, its skin tough and shiny. Alchemists and assassins alike will pay for it, though it must be handled with great care.

747106.name: candle black cultist wax
747106.room_desc: A thick black candle stands here, its wick charred.
747106.description: A fat candle of black wax, carved with a spider and a ring of tiny, cramped letters. It burns with a smoky, greenish flame and smells of rot and myrrh.
